title: Guild Contracts
description: There is always something chalked on the board for members who have earned the standing - theft, smuggling, a debt, a message with weight behind it. Whatever it is today, the shape does not change. Look at the mark, take what is named, come back.

objectives.description: Case whatever the board has pinned up today
Take the thing the contract names and nothing else
Go back to the board and chalk the contract off

job_types.title: Simple Theft
job_types.description: Steal a specific item from a random location

job_types.title: Smuggling Run
job_types.description: Transport contraband between cities without detection

objectives.description: Deliver without being caught by guards

job_types.title: Debt Collection
job_types.description: Collect a debt owed to the Guild from a reluctant debtor

job_types.title: Reconnaissance
job_types.description: Scout a location and report security details for future jobs

job_types.title: Send a Message
job_types.description: Intimidate someone causing problems for Guild operations

job_types.title: Professional Burglary
job_types.description: Break into a secured building and steal everything valuable
job_types.failure_consequences: Guards alerted, potential combat or escape

generation_rules.selection: Random job type based on player rank
generation_rules.target_randomization: Random location and target from available lists
generation_rules.difficulty_scaling: Higher ranks get harder variants with better rewards

notes: Repeatable quest system. Six job types with varying difficulty. Random generation from target/location pools. Scales with player rank. Contract board in Guild hideout, Dalhurst. FIXED: this file used to have no top-level 'objectives' array at all - the job_types entries carry their own nested lists, and nothing in the engine reads job_types - so it parsed to a quest with zero objectives and completed the instant it was accepted. It now carries a real three-beat objectives array in the rotating petty-job shape the sibling repeatables use (adventurers_repeatable_bounty, mercenary_repeatable_contracts), drawing its targets from its own job_types blocks: `recon_target` from reconnaissance, `contract_item` from simple_theft, and the board itself for the turn-in. job_types and rank_bonuses are kept as authored design for the generator that will re-skin those three beats. `repeatable: true` and `cooldown_hours: 24` were also dead - the engine reads neither, only `cooldown_days` - so the 24 hours is now written as cooldown_days: 1, which is what the engine can actually honour.
